card.category: Spanish-language reseller of resold AllDebrid credentials (12-month SKU)
card.summary: None. The product is a paid 12-month credential; no trial or free allowance is offered by the seller.

record.category: Spanish-language reseller of resold AllDebrid credentials (12-month SKU)

free_tier.stated: None. The product is a paid 12-month credential; no trial or free allowance is offered by the seller.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the underlying service is AllDebrid, whose own host and file caps apply.

retention.stated: 12 months: 'Cuenta Premium AllDebrid, 12 meses'. The page does not say when the 12 months start, so a credential already running when it is sold would deliver less than a year.

egress.terms: The seller publishes no traffic terms. The credential inherits AllDebrid's terms, which the seller restates only as marketing: 'Maxima velocidad de descarga', 'Descargas sin periodos de espera, sin captchas ni publicidad'.

record.interface_detail: The buyer gets AllDebrid account details and uses AllDebrid's own panel and API. The seller ships no client.
record.tooling: AllDebrid's API works because the credential is a real AllDebrid account. The seller names JDownloader, MEGAsync, MiPony and IDM as the intended clients.
record.chaining: A 12-month resold credential is the longest single payment among debrid providers, which makes the seller's survival part of the product. It chains with Stremio and torrent add-ons like any AllDebrid account.

limits.value: the seller's own rule: 'La cuenta es para uso exclusivo en una sola IP' and two devices only if they share the same connection, 'pero su uso no puede ser simultaneo'

record.limits_note: The seller states the enforcement explicitly: 'de haber anomalias en estos puntos, la cuenta se bloqueara y se suspendera el servicio sin derecho a devolucion o garantia de reactivacion'. That is a one-IP, non-simultaneous credential sold to an unknown number of buyers.
record.binding_note: Nothing about bytes decides this product; the account dies the first time two buyers open it from different addresses, which the seller's own rule anticipates.
record.price_per_tb_month: USD 900.00 as stated by the seller, currency not printed on the page; not metered per TB

identity_cost.detail: A Wix store order with an email address.

record.reliability_note: The credential is registered by the seller, cannot be re-keyed by the buyer, is pinned to one IP, and blocks without refund on a rule breach. The seller's support promise ('Brindamos soporte tecnico ante cualquier anomalia y durante todo el tiempo contratado') is the only recourse for a 12-month term.
record.confidence_note: Price, term, the no-credential-change rule, the single-IP rule and the block-without-refund clause were read on the seller's page. The currency is unverified: the page prints '$900.00' with no currency code and no country, so no USD conversion is offered.

evidence.proved: 'No se pueden modificar los datos de registro (Como configuraciones, usuario o contrasena)' and 'La cuenta es para uso exclusivo en una sola IP'
'la cuenta se bloqueara y se suspendera el servicio sin derecho a devolucion o garantia de reactivacion' - the enforcement and the absence of recourse

record.notes: This is the cleanest written statement of the shared-credential model found in either language: the seller names the three things that break it - no re-keying, one IP, no simultaneous use - and prices a 12-month term against them. If '$900.00' is Mexican pesos the product is about USD 48; if it is US dollars it is twenty times the direct annual price.

extras.currency_status: unstated on the page; no conversion attempted
extras.possible_readings: MXN 900 at 18.7613 would be USD 47.97; USD 900 would be USD 900.00; ARS 900 at 1550 would be USD 0.58 and is implausible for a 12-month SKU
